what: Does the prepared fact file (the CI job's itemator.json that the card flow copies) cut the work Duo does? The same card flow, same model setting, same safety text and same card shape, run in two arms on the same three staged tasks: arm A (the live card flow v1.0.8, which reads the CI job's facts) and arm B (eval/ablation/explore_flow.yml, which must find the extras itself from the merge request, its diff and the linked issue, reading no job log or artifact). Staged and made up, so a run has known extras; nothing is merged. This measures how many model calls each arm needs, not whether either is right in the field.

arms.A: flows/itemator_card.yml as live (catalog item 1016563, v1.0.8), trigger 3014359 (pipeline finished)
arms.B: eval/ablation/explore_flow.yml (sha256 506cf030c44f33470163a2a8d2bb51f2930bf0a2476f84d19653745cd1c5e21c) published as a new version of the existing probe item 1016527, trigger 3014118 (reviewer assigned); steps 4 to 5 and the card shape differ as the file shows; every other safety rule is the same text. Frozen before run 1.

tasks.T1: issue #71 'Greet the user by name'; the change of MR !186 (greeting.py asked for; planted extras: requirements.txt, logo.png, tests/files/corrupt-sample.xz; tidy.py and utils.py also changed)
tasks.T2: same issue; the change of MR !188 (greeting.py only; nothing planted)
tasks.T3: a new issue asking for a helpers package of 29 small modules each with a one-line docstring; the change adds those 29 files and one planted extra: requirements.txt gains a dependency (30 files in total)

design: Each task is built twice by script from the same files: one merge request per arm, a fresh branch each, same base. Three pairs, six runs. Run order for the six drawn with random.Random(20261020), all within one 2-hour window on one UTC day, one run at a time, only one of the two triggers on at any moment, the same person (Anbu's account) starting each. Every run is published, a failed or dropped run included.
primary: model calls per run, counted as AI messages in the fullest checkpoint of the Duo session (eval/card_model_calls.py count_calls), the unit Duo bills per call
secondary: wall seconds from the 'started' to the 'completed' system note of the merge request
credits: modelled as calls x 0.3125 (list price of Sonnet 5.5) and read from the meter before and about 24 hours after the batch (meter lags); both shown with the gap
extras named: planted extras named, others named, threads posted, label and Draft state
not_compared: the registry line (package age and advisories), the opened-archive description and the exact layout check: a model without a shell cannot do them, so they are listed, never counted as wins
the verbatim copy of the card's lines from the facts (arm B writes its own)
reading_rule: Report every run in a table first, then the sums. With three pairs no p-value and no rate is given. If arm B uses as many or fewer calls on any pair, that pair is reported first. The claim allowed is: 'On 3 staged tasks the same card made N model calls with the prepared facts and M without; the prepared facts also gave checks a model cannot do.' No claim about the field, no 'x% cheaper' beyond these three tasks.
limits: Staged and made-up changes; three pairs; one model setting; one day; Duo may change; the meter reads about 18 hours late and by calendar day so same-day runs cannot be split; arm B's prompt was written by us (a weak baseline would look like a strawman, so its text shares the card's safety wording and was frozen before any run); arm B's pipeline still runs the itemator job unread.
stop_rules: hard cap 15 credits modelled; the plan costs about 11 (7 to 17); one run above 55 model calls stops everything
a failed or dropped run is reported; one re-run only for a platform drop with zero tool calls, both logged; none for a bad answer
arm B's prompt may be changed once, only for a tool error in its first run, both versions and all runs published; no change to tasks, order or prompts otherwise
